summary: No Moscow Oblast-specific law, enforcement action, institution or documented incident appears in the sources reviewed. Russia's national framework governs the oblast in full, and the national assessment applies to visitors and residents here without any regional variation the evidence supports.
tangentialFactors: The national sources available, the UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (June 2025) and Human Rights Watch's report of 30 June 2025 on extremism designations, give enforcement totals for Russia as a whole and do not break them down by federal subject. No figure for prosecutions, detentions or incidents in Moscow Oblast can be derived from them, so the oblast cannot be ranked against other regions on the available evidence.
localsOnly: Residents of Moscow Oblast live under the same national legal regime as the rest of Russia. The sources identify no regional anti-discrimination provision, no regional protection mechanism and no regional enforcement practice specific to the oblast.
outOfScopeNotes: Unresolved: whether Moscow Oblast police, prosecutors and courts apply the national statutes at a rate above or below the national average. No regional court statistics, regional police guidance, or municipal rules on facilities and service access were located. The absence of oblast-level reporting is not evidence of lower enforcement.
